title: How the adaptive LoRA system routes a prompt
subtitle: A learned router picks a specialist LoRA adapter, a GPU engine generates with it, and a self-evaluator scores it.

nodes.label: User
nodes.detail: Sends a prompt from the Gradio demo or the API, either naming an adapter or leaving the choice to the router.
nodes.tradeoff: The hosted Gradio demo uses keyword routing and Llama 3.1 8B on Groq with one system prompt per adapter, not the trained adapters.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.detail: Identifies the caller by API key or IP, allows 60 requests a minute, and forwards the prompt to a Modal serverless GPU endpoint.
nodes.tradeoff: A circuit breaker opens after 5 failures and waits 60 seconds before trying the GPU again.

nodes.label: Response cache
nodes.detail: Keeps responses by prompt and adapter for one hour, up to 1,000 entries, evicting the oldest first.
nodes.tradeoff: It lives in memory; the code notes Redis as the production choice.

nodes.label: Learned router
nodes.detail: A small BERT encoder with heads that predict adapter weights, query complexity (easy, medium, hard) and confidence. Adapters above 0.1 weight are used.

nodes.label: Adapter registry
nodes.detail: Specialist adapters such as reasoning, code and analysis are registered with metadata and loaded onto the base model with PEFT, or merged into it.
nodes.tradeoff: The README claims 4 GB of GPU memory against 16 GB for its single-adapter baseline.

nodes.label: GPU inference
nodes.detail: A vLLM engine serves the base model and attaches the chosen LoRA adapter per request, with up to 4 adapters of rank 64 or less.
nodes.tradeoff: The Modal T4 deployment keeps one container warm but, for now, serves the 4-bit base model under every adapter name.

nodes.label: GPU cluster
nodes.detail: A Deployment runs 2 replicas with one NVIDIA GPU each, and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler scales between 2 and 10.
nodes.tradeoff: The README prices Kubernetes at $100+ a month against about $0.001 a request on Modal.

nodes.label: Self-evaluator
nodes.detail: Scores relevance, factuality, coherence, safety and uncertainty, weighted 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15 and 0.1. Below 0.6 counts as a failure.
nodes.tradeoff: It can also ask an OpenAI or Anthropic model to judge, when those keys are set.

nodes.label: Monitoring
nodes.detail: Prometheus collects request, token and latency metrics for Grafana dashboards; a drift detector compares new query embeddings with a baseline.
nodes.tradeoff: An alert fires when average adapter inference time stays above 5 seconds for 5 minutes.

flow.text: Asks for a Python binary search function.
Checks the rate limit, misses the cache, and forwards the prompt.
Encodes the prompt and gives the code adapter the most weight.
Supplies the code adapter's LoRA weights.
Generates with the base model plus the code adapter.
Combines relevance, coherence, factuality and safety into one weighted score.
Records latency and checks the query embedding for drift.
Gets the answer and the name of the adapter that wrote it.

takeaways.text: Gumbel-Softmax keeps adapter choice differentiable in training, so the router learns from data rather than keyword rules.
QLoRA trains each adapter on a 4-bit NF4 base model with double quantization to cut GPU memory.
Answers under a 0.6 weighted score are stored as failure patterns; the README ties these to targeted synthetic data.
